title: OA ChatCompletions bidirectional request/response shaper
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement a robust bidirectional mapping layer that translates Redwood inference API requests/responses to and from the OpenAI Chat Completions (OA CC) shape. Scope includes streaming framing semantics, tool/function call signal translation, structured output (JSON schema) enforcement, and error/edge-case normalization. This ticket delivers the runtime adapter plus a compatibility suite (unit + integration tests) and a staged rollout plan. Acceptance criteria: 1) Redwood API callers can use OA CC request shapes (messages / functions / temperature / max_tokens / user) with identical results to native Redwood call patterns for common cases; 2) Streaming responses from upstream OA-style sources get mapped into Redwood streaming frames without violating chunk boundaries or losing function call tokens; 3) Function/tool calls emitted by OA models are exposed to Redwood tooling with canonical call object {name, arguments} and mapped back when calling downstream tools; 4) Structured output proposals (schema enforcement) are converted between OA content fields and Redwood structured metadata fields; 5) Backwards-compatible error mapping (OA error codes -> Redwood error codes) and surface-level rate/usage metadata preserved.
decision_record: Chose a thin adapter layer in the API gateway that performs: (a) request normalization (expand/flatten legacy fields, translate functions->tool spec), (b) streaming re-framing (buffer short-lived tokens and emit Redwood event types), and (c) canonical response enrichment (attach mapping metadata header). Reason: minimal runtime overhead, single point to maintain compatibility, and easier rollback. Rejected option: deep changes in serving runtime to accept dual shapes — that would increase risk and coupling with model IO paths.
implementation_notes: Components: 1) Request normalizer module (stateless) with a ruleset that maps OA fields to Redwood fields and validates functions/tool definitions; 2) Stream shaper that uses a sliding-window tokenizer sentinel to ensure function call boundaries are preserved when chunking; 3) Response canonicalizer that emits both Redwood-native and OA-compatible envelope metadata when operate-in-compat mode is enabled; 4) Feature flag gate: compatibility_mode=oa_chatcompletions to allow gradual rollout. Implementation will live under services/gateway/compat/oa_cc_shaper with feature tests in infra/tests/compat/.
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping rules (100+ examples covering messages, roles, name/user fields, function definitions, and argument shapes). Integration harness that spins up a mock OA endpoint to stream SSE-style chunks, validating that Redwood streaming consumer observers receive identical reconstructed token stream and that function call events are emitted exactly once. End-to-end test matrix: synchronous CC, streaming CC, function-calling success/failure, schema-enforced structured outputs, and error mapping. Add property tests to fuzz malformed OA payloads to assert graceful NACK and mapped error codes.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; 2) Canary release to internal staging orgs (5% traffic) and run reproducibility tests for 48h; 3) Expand to 25% while monitoring structured-output regression rates, latency P95 delta, and function call fidelity; 4) Full rollout after 7 days with no regressions. Rollback: flip feature flag to disable compatibility_mode which will stop OA-shaped requests at gateway and return an advisory response to callers.
monitoring: Add per-route histograms for latency P50/P95, counts for mapping_errors, function_call_events_emitted, and schema_validation_failures. Dashboard: compatibility/oa_cc_shaper with alerts: mapping_errors > 0.1% of requests sustained for 15m, function_call_misfires > 0.05% over 1h. Add tracing tags: compat.layer=oa_cc_shaper and mapping.rule_version=<semver> to correlate with deploys.
risks: 1) Streaming re-framing could increase tail latency if buffer windows misconfigured. 2) Mis-mapped function arguments could break customer tool integrations. 3) Over-zealous schema enforcement may surface false positives for models that return near-JSON outputs. Mitigations: conservative defaults (small buffer), opt-in schema enforcement, and roll-forward fixes with clear mapping versioning.
